title: Maximum EMF expression
description: Essential: The response must correctly state the maximum induced EMF as Em = nBSω, leading to the numerical value 200√2 V.

title: Instantaneous EMF expression
description: Essential: The response must provide the complete instantaneous EMF expression e = 200√2 sin(100t) V, including correct amplitude, angular frequency, and sine function.

title: Voltmeter reading calculation
description: Essential: The response must correctly calculate the RMS voltage from the maximum EMF, giving the voltmeter reading as 200 V.

title: Transformer ratio application
description: Important: The response must correctly apply the transformer turns ratio (2:1) to relate primary and secondary RMS voltages and currents.

title: Resistor value from Ohm's law
description: Important: The response must use the secondary circuit's RMS voltage and the given ammeter reading (2 A) with Ohm's law to find R = 25 Ω.

title: Sine vs cosine function
description: Pitfall: Penalize if the instantaneous EMF uses cosine instead of sine, given the timing starts when the coil is at the neutral plane.

title: RMS vs peak confusion
description: Pitfall: Penalize if the voltmeter reading is incorrectly given as the peak voltage (200√2 V) instead of the RMS value.

title: Transformer power conservation
description: Optional: The solution may explicitly state or use the conservation of power (ideal transformer) as part of the reasoning for part (3).
